title: Vendor selection
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's get started. I've been looking at our options for a cloud infrastructure provider, and I'd like to hear everyone's thoughts.

SRE: I've been worried about AWS's downtime incidents in the past.

CTO: I understand your concern, but we've also seen that AWS support has consistently performed well based on our trial period data.

Finance Partner: Yes, I've been crunching the numbers, and AWS offers the best cost-benefit. Google Cloud Platform has a higher long-term cost due to their data egress fees.

Platform Engineering Lead: Exactly, and Microsoft Azure isn't the best fit for us since it has limited integration with our existing on-premises systems.

SRE: And what about IBM Cloud? Haven't we overlooked that?

Platform Engineering Lead: To be honest, IBM Cloud is not yet on the table due to limited knowledge about their offerings.

CTO: Given our existing usage of AWS S3 storage, migrating to AWS will incur minimal costs. Plus, their features fit well with our current data management workflow.

SRE: Still, I can't shake off the doubts about AWS's stability.

Finance Partner: I agree that we'll have to invest in training our staff to become proficient in AWS tools, but that's a one-time cost.

Platform Engineering Lead: And remember, we'll need to reconsider our cloud provider if integration issues arise post-acquisition.

SRE: I can live with that, but I'll keep an eye on AWS's performance.

CTO: I think we've made our decision. Adopt AWS for cloud infrastructure.

Finance Partner: Agreed.

Platform Engineering Lead: I'll take ownership of this. Let's plan the migration strategically.

CTO: I sign off on this decision.

*During a brief moment of levity*

Platform Engineering Lead: By the way, did you guys hear about the latest cat videos trending online?

SRE: I've been meaning to catch up on those. The office has been so busy lately.

Finance Partner: I'll have to admit, I don't understand the fuss, but it seems they've got the whole internet purring.

CTO: Well, it's a nice break from the cloud talks. Let's get back to work.

Title: Adoption of AWS for Cloud Infrastructure

The team has decided to transition to Amazon Web Services (AWS) for our cloud infrastructure. This move will incur minimal migration costs given our current use of AWS S3 storage.

Discussed during the meeting were the limitations of Microsoft Azure in integrating with our existing on-premises systems.

Key stakeholders involved include the Platform Engineering Lead and CTO.

The decision was made based on AWS's compatibility with our current data management workflow, and the positive performance data from our AWS trial period. Staff training in AWS tools will be required post-adoption.

Furthermore, AWS support has consistently demonstrated high performance levels. Future integration issues with potential acquiring companies will be re-evaluated as necessary.

No discussion was logged about the cost comparison with Google Cloud Platform, IBM Cloud, concerns about AWS downtime incidents, or the need for post-acquisition reconsideration of cloud providers.
